item.title: Contingency plans being prepared as El Niño threatens water supply
item.description: Contingency plans are being prepared to respond to the expected impacts of a severe El Niño event, including worsening water shortages in parts of Fiji. Director of the National Disaster Risk Management Office, Napolioni Boseiwaqa says humanitarian clusters have been instructed to prepare their contingency plans, which are now being collated before being presented to Cabinet.
item.content:encoded:
Contingency plans are being prepared to respond to the expected impacts of a severe El Niño event, including worsening water shortages in parts of Fiji.

Director of the National Disaster Risk Management Office, Napolioni Boseiwaqa says humanitarian clusters have been instructed to prepare their contingency plans, which are now being collated before being presented to Cabinet.

Boseiwaqa says the preparations follow warnings from the Fiji Meteorological Service of a possible severe El Niño event, with below-normal rainfall expected from now until early February next year.

Insert: NDRMO - Attended to right now Sept 17

Boseiwaqa says maritime islands and other areas that rely on rainfall or boreholes are particularly vulnerable because they do not have sustainable water sources.

He says Taveuni is among the areas currently requiring assistance, with water-carting being arranged after communities reported low water supplies.

Boseiwaqa says while the Water Authority of Fiji has a supply in the area, there have reportedly been issues affecting the water system.

He says as an alternative, arrangements have been made with Government Shipping to transport water to the affected area, with supplies expected by the weekend.

Boseiwaqa says the current forecast indicates that most parts of Fiji could experience the impacts of El Niño in the coming months, including the western parts of Viti Levu, as well as northern, eastern and parts of the Central Division.

He says Fiji is currently experiencing meteorological drought due to below-normal rainfall.

Boseiwaqa says this could progress to hydrological drought as groundwater supplies decline, followed by agricultural drought affecting crops and livestock.

He says the impacts could eventually extend to food security and health.

Boseiwaqa says the NDRMO is working with technical agencies, including Energy Fiji Limited and the Water Authority of Fiji, to assess the situation and determine the measures required as Fiji prepares for the anticipated impacts of El Niño.

item.title: Court dismisses Panapasa's application to vacate trial
item.description: Suva Magistrate Charles Ratakele has dismissed an application by lawyer Simone Seruvakula to vacate the trial of former Acting Commissioner of Corrections Salote Panapasa and set a new trial date. The application followed Panapasa’s former lawyer, Vinisoni Filipe withdrawing from representing her on the day of the trial this week.
item.content:encoded:
Suva Magistrate Charles Ratakele has dismissed an application by lawyer Simone Seruvakula to vacate the trial of former Acting Commissioner of Corrections Salote Panapasa and set a new trial date.

The application followed Panapasa’s former lawyer, Vinisoni Filipe withdrawing from representing her on the day of the trial this week.

Magistrate Ratakele ruled that the application did not establish a good cause to postpone the trial.

He noted that 11 witnesses had already been summoned to give evidence.

The trial is now scheduled to begin on Monday. Panapasa faces two counts of abuse of office and an alternative charge of general dishonesty causing a loss. It is alleged that between August 1st and September 30th, 2023, Panapasa, while being employed as a civil servant in Suva, instructed officers to facilitate the use of Corrections building materials for her private residence in Kinoya. It is also alleged that between August 1st and October 31st, 2023, Panapasa instructed a Corrections officer to alter the weekly reports to justify the use of the building materials at her home.

item.title: Three men charged over alleged Nabua taxi robbery to appear in court today
item.description: Three men alleged to have robbed a taxi driver along Sukanaivalu Road in Nabua on Sunday will appear in court today for their bail application. The men allegedly hired the taxi from Narere to Nabua and, when they reached their destination, allegedly stole the driver’s watch and cash.
item.content:encoded:
Three men alleged to have robbed a taxi driver along Sukanaivalu Road in Nabua on Sunday will appear in court today for their bail application.

The men allegedly hired the taxi from Narere to Nabua and, when they reached their destination, allegedly stole the driver’s watch and cash.

They were arrested shortly after the alleged incident by the Southern Division Task Force.

The three have been jointly charged with one count each of aggravated robbery and serious assault.

They appeared at the Suva Magistrates Court on Wednesday and were remanded until today, when their bail application will be heard.
